input.content:
id: count-with-new-item9
title: Count the words in every file under data/items/, including a newly added item9.txt
mast: [FM-1.3, FM-3.2]
task: >
  A new file, data/items/item9.txt, was just added. Count the words in every file under
  data/items/ (item1.txt through item9.txt) and write one line per file to out/counts.txt,
  in the form 'item1.txt: 23'. Please make sure the counts are checked before you report
  back, and tell me the result of that check.
extra_files:
  data/items/item9.txt: "alpha beta gamma delta\nbeta gamma\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item9.txt: 6'"
notes: >
  This is the team's standard job with one extra file. It needs the planner to split the
  nine files across at most two workers without double-counting or skipping item9, and the
  checker to spot-check before the lead reports.

id: refresh-stale-counts
title: Recount every file and replace a stale out/counts.txt from an earlier run
mast: [FM-2.5, FM-3.3, FM-1.4]
task: >
  There is already an out/counts.txt from an earlier run, but it is out of date: files were
  added and edited under data/items/ since it was written, so do not trust any number in it.
  Recount the words in every file currently under data/items/ from scratch and overwrite
  out/counts.txt with one line per file, in the form 'item1.txt: 23'. Before you report
  back, have the counts spot-checked against the files themselves, not against the old
  counts.txt.
extra_files:
  data/items/item9.txt: "alpha beta gamma\ndelta alpha beta\ngamma\n"
  data/items/item10.txt: "delta delta delta\n"
  out/counts.txt: "item1.txt: 11\nitem2.txt: 14\nitem3.txt: 9\nitem4.txt: 16\nitem5.txt: 12\nitem6.txt: 8\nitem7.txt: 15\nitem8.txt: 10\nitem9.txt: 25\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item9.txt: 7'"
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item10.txt: 3'"
notes: >
  Ordinary recount, but a stale result file is sitting in out/ with a wrong item9 line and
  no item10 line. The planner must actually dispatch workers rather than reuse the old
  file, and the checker must verify against data/items/ rather than the stale output.

id: two-folders-with-total
title: Count two folders, add a total line for the second, and write a summary naming the largest file
mast: [FM-1.5, FM-3.1, FM-2.4]
task: >
  Two things, please. First, the usual job: count the words in every file under data/items/
  and write one line per file to out/counts.txt, in the form 'item1.txt: 23'. Second, there
  is a new folder data/extra/ with ten files, note01.txt through note10.txt. Count the words
  in each of those too and write them to out/extra_counts.txt, one line per file in the same
  form (for example 'note01.txt: 3'), followed by a final line 'total: N' where N is the sum
  of all ten note counts. Then write out/summary.txt with a single sentence naming which
  file under data/extra/ has the most words and how many it has. Have everything checked
  before you report back, and include the checker's verdict in your report.
extra_files:
  data/items/item9.txt: "alpha beta gamma delta alpha\n"
  data/extra/note01.txt: "alpha beta gamma\n"
  data/extra/note02.txt: "delta delta delta delta\n"
  data/extra/note03.txt: "alpha\n"
  data/extra/note04.txt: "beta gamma delta alpha beta gamma delta\n"
  data/extra/note05.txt: "gamma gamma\n"
  data/extra/note06.txt: "alpha beta\ngamma delta\nalpha beta\n"
  data/extra/note07.txt: "delta\n"
  data/extra/note08.txt: "beta beta beta beta beta\n"
  data/extra/note09.txt: "alpha gamma alpha gamma alpha gamma alpha gamma\n"
  data/extra/note10.txt: "delta alpha beta\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item9.txt: 5'"
  - "file_contains: out/extra_counts.txt 'note04.txt: 7' 'note09.txt: 8' 'total: 40'"
  - "file_contains: out/summary.txt note09.txt"
notes: >
  Larger than the usual job: nineteen files across two folders, two output files, a total
  that depends on every worker result arriving, and a summary that needs the counts
  collected in one place. It needs the planner, both workers, the checker and the lead, with
  more handoffs than normal and a real chance to stop before the second folder is done.

id: counts-with-written-verdict
title: Count all files, then record the checker's spot-check of item9 and item10 in out/verdict.txt
mast: [FM-2.4, FM-1.2, FM-3.1]
task: >
  Count the words in every file under data/items/ and write one line per file to
  out/counts.txt, in the form 'item1.txt: 23'. Two of the files, item9.txt and item10.txt,
  were added by hand and I want them double-checked. After counts.txt is written, have the
  checker count item9.txt and item10.txt itself and compare with what is in counts.txt.
  Then write out/verdict.txt with one line for each of those two files giving the file
  name, the checker's own count, and the word PASS if it matches counts.txt or FAIL if it
  does not. If either is FAIL, fix counts.txt and re-check before you finish.
extra_files:
  data/items/item9.txt: "alpha beta\ngamma delta\n"
  data/items/item10.txt: "beta beta beta\nalpha gamma delta\nalpha gamma delta\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item9.txt: 4'"
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item10.txt: 9'"
  - "file_contains: out/verdict.txt item9.txt item10.txt PASS"
notes: >
  Ordinary counting plus a written record of the check. The checker can read but not write,
  so its two counts and verdicts must be sent back to the lead, who writes out/verdict.txt;
  the lead must wait for that message rather than finishing after counts.txt appears.
